views.chatgpt.intro.en: Ask for work in a ChatGPT chat: “file a request to change my opening hours”, “how is my site request doing?”. It uses your own ChatGPT plan, and it can do what you can do here, nothing more. What it files waits for Ali like any other request.

views.chatgpt.step3.en: ChatGPT sends you here to sign in. Approve it, and it shows up on this card.

views.assistants.intro.en: Claude, Cursor, or any assistant that speaks MCP. It sees your projects, files requests, replies and sets budgets: the same things you can do here, nothing more. Its requests wait for Ali like any other.

views.newKey.subtitle.en: Name it so you know which key to revoke later.

views.showKey.hint.en: The assistant sends the key as "Authorization: Bearer …".

views.github.intro.en: Keep a project's code in your own GitHub account, or let us work on an existing private repo. You pick exactly which repos the app can reach, and can revoke it any time on GitHub.

views.github.disconnectText.en: Projects using this connection lose access to the repos it reached. You can reconnect any time by installing the app again.

views.cloudflare.intro.en: Have your sites hosted in your own Cloudflare account instead of ours: Cloudflare bills you directly, and a small site usually fits its free plan. Connecting changes nothing by itself: no site moves to your account until you ask for it. On Cloudflare you choose which account to share, and you can revoke it there or here any time.

ticket.now.approved.next.en: It starts as soon as a machine is free. Details you add now reach the agent before it starts.

ticket.now.in_progress.next.en: It works on a sealed copy of your project; nothing live is touched. Replies you send now are read before it ships.

offer.step.request.body.en: Sign in with your email and write what you need: in the portal, by email, or in the chat below. No call to get started.

offer.step.approve.body.en: I read every request myself. Nothing starts until I say so, and I tell you if it is the wrong thing to build.

offer.step.build.body.en: An AI agent does the typing in a sealed copy of your project. It cannot publish, deploy, or touch anything live.

offer.step.ship.body.en: I check the result before it goes anywhere. How closely is your call: a quick check that it runs, or every changed line. You follow it all in one thread.

pricing.attention.auto.what.en: The agent does the work. I approve the request and check that it runs. I do not read every line.

pricing.attention.auto.for.en: Text and style changes, small fixes, anything easy to undo

pricing.attention.checked.what.en: The agent does the work and I read every changed line before it ships.

pricing.attention.checked.for.en: New pages, forms, features, anything customers touch

pricing.attention.hands_on.what.en: I work on it with the agent: decisions, hard problems, advice.

pricing.attention.hands_on.for.en: Architecture, debugging the weird one, consultation

site.home.title.en: M. Ali Petek — software help by the minute, not by a quote

site.home.description.en: Vibe coded most of it? Get developer help with the last mile, billed by the second. You send a request, Ali approves it, an AI agent builds it, and he checks it before anything ships.

site.home.shelf.note.en: {n, plural, one {# thing} other {# things}} I built and still answer for. Proof there is a developer behind the agent.

site.home.shelf.empty.en: Nothing on this shelf with that label.

site.home.work.hint.en: Hover a stop, or tab through and press, to read the damage.

offer.priceHook.en: A one-minute fix is {price}. No quote, no minimum.

offer.tagline.en: You vibe code most of it. I take the last mile — the bug, the deploy, the payments — billed by the second.

offer.priceNote.en: ${rate} an hour of my time, billed by the second; the AI at cost, no markup.

offer.priceRule.en: You pay for the time I actually spend, billed by the second, plus what the AI run cost, with no markup. No packages, no minimum.

offer.priceWhy.en: The less of me a job needs, the less it costs. A change the agent finishes on its own is a minute or two of my time. You choose how closely I look, and you can set a budget I will not pass without asking.

offer.serverless.body.en: What I build runs serverless. There is no server to patch or resize, and a traffic spike is not a migration project.

offer.who.en: For business owners who need software work done, not a development team to manage.

offer.why.yourself.answer.en: Do — most of it. When it stalls at the last mile, send me that part. A one-minute fix is {price} of my time, and you never wait for a quote.

offer.why.chatgpt.answer.en: It writes code. It does not put it in your project, run it, or answer for it. Here the agent does the typing and a developer approves the job before it starts and checks it before you see it.

offer.why.agency.answer.en: No quote, no call, no minimum invoice. A small fix does not wait until it is worth someone's afternoon: it is {price} of my time.

offer.why.cheapest.instead.en: the cheapest developer you can find

offer.why.cheapest.answer.en: On small jobs this is cheaper, because the agent does the hours and you pay for my minutes. And the person who signs off is the one you write to.

offer.safeguard.1.en: Nothing starts until I approve the request.

offer.safeguard.2.en: The agent works on a sealed copy of your project. It cannot publish, deploy, or touch anything live.

offer.safeguard.3.en: Set a budget and I will not pass it without asking.

offer.safeguard.4.en: If a machine stops mid-job, the job goes back in the queue instead of stalling.

offer.safeguard.5.en: Every message, change and decision is in one thread you can read.

site.home.kb.foot.en: Every problem my agents hit, and what actually fixed it — public, searchable, and mountable by your own agent at malipetek.dev/mcp.

site.home.plugins.foot.en: I build these for my own harness and publish them to npm as @malipetek packages. Install one with “dsh plugin add <name>”, or read the whole set at malipetek.dev/plugins.
